_about: THE alert copy of every platform (#42), en + es: an alert notification's title, body and actions, and every mute /
remind-less state line. Android words it from its string resources (monitor AlertCopy, designsystem MuteText;
AlertCopyTest checks every case in en and es), the Mac from AlertText (notifications, AlertCopyTests) and MuteCopy
(lines, MuteCopyTests in en and es). A case with `platform` is that platform's only (the Mac's input
placeholder and send button, Android's direct-reply label); `en_mac` / `es_mac` = the Mac's wording of the same words. `device`: what
'this phone' / 'this Mac' says.
Lines (round f31; the user, 2026-10-22: 'muted alerts should show a countdown, and the Never option makes no sense …
figure out the best copywriting'): wording after AOSP Do Not Disturb (core/res zen_mode_forever 'Until you turn off'
/ 'Hasta que lo desactives', zen_mode_until 'Until %1$s', zen_mode_duration_hours 'For 1 hour' / 'Durante 1 hora').
Durations through Durations.text (lines) and Durations.compact (the card pill). 'side' = the side's alerts: low
(very low too), high (very high, extremely high too), falling_fast, rising_fast, no_data. Side names (the owner, 2026-11-14: 'Low alerts
muted' can simply be 'Lows muted'): Lows, Highs, Falling fast, Rising fast, No data; es Bajas, Altas, Bajadas rápidas, Subidas
rápidas, Alertas sin datos (plural nouns, so 'silenciadas' agrees). 'side_after' (round f33): a quiet rule after
carbs / rapid insulin ('treatment'), worded like a mute and counting down to the rule's end; 'side_falling': the
falling-back-into-range rule (no end); 'side_rising' (#193): its low-side mirror, rising back into range (no end). es 'queda' / 'quedan' agree with the duration (one unit of 1: queda).
Notifications (SPEC §1 'Headline'): 'headline' = the title, without 'glucose' (the owner, 2026-11-14: 'it's obvious it's glucose') (kind, treated: the answering treatments acknowledged);
'body' = the value and arrow in the person's unit (mg/dL or mmol/L, the language's decimal separator), the rate for
the fast kinds, the sensor's LO / HI as such, for no data when the last reading came and its value ('ageMin' since
it; a time never goes out of date on a notification left up, #195) or 'No reading yet' when the source never
delivered one, 'No recent reading' when a level alert has no reading. The body shows the newest reading while the
alert is up (#195): 'ageS' = its age when posted; once late (over 90 s) its time follows, from 5 min (stale) the
ring replaces the arrow and the fast kinds drop their rate (Android also strikes the value through, as the card).
'{time}' = the reading's time as the card writes it (Freshness.timeText: 14:05, Tue 14:05, 12 Oct).
'action' = the notification's buttons, in this order: 'treatment' (opens Add treatment focused on carbs for the low
side, rapid insulin for the high side; every kind but no data, where the device can add entries), 'remind_less' /
'remind_as_usual', then 'mute'; a muted note offers 'treatment' (its side) and 'unmute' only (the person unmutes and
mutes again; no 'Change time'). No action has an ellipsis on any platform (the owner's review, 2026-11-14: Treatment
opens a dialog without one, so the ellipsis meant nothing). 'Mute', not 'Mute for': a button is a short verb that
names the result (Android's notification action guidance; Apple HIG notifications: 'a short, title-case name that
clearly describes the result'); the length comes from its chips, its input label or its sheet.
'mute_choice_spoken' = what TalkBack says for a Mute chip.
'all_scope' (#42, UX review: 'Mute all copy should say what it covers'): under Mute all's line on the device.
'headline_escalated' (#39): a follower's title for the wearer's very low nobody answered on the wearer's phone.
'night' (#38): while the night alerts apply, the line every surface that shows alert states says, with the clock
time they end (the platform's clock formatter).
